title: Mujadara
subtitle: Lebanese lentils and rice with caramelised onions
excerpt: Mujadara is a study in patience at two points: the lentils need a 20-minute head start before the rice joins them, and the onions need at least 25 minutes over low heat to turn properly golden and sweet. Get both right and the finished dish is deeply satisfying.
sourceNotes: Mujadara is one of the oldest recorded recipes in the world, appearing in a thirteenth-century Arabic cookery manuscript. It is a staple of Levantine cuisine and known across the region by slight variations of the same name. The caramelised onions are always served on top and are, for many, the best part of the dish.

content.text: The caramelised onion topping is cooked separately in a wide frying pan while the lentils and rice simmer in the pot. They take longer than you think -- do not rush them or you will have softened onion rather than a deeply sweet, golden tangle.

items.prepNote: 2 thinly sliced for caramelising, 1 finely diced for the base

content.text: Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the cumin seeds, ground cumin, cinnamon, and allspice and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed lentils and 900 ml of cold water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook uncovered for 20 minutes until the lentils are just tender but still holding their shape.
Add the rice and 1 tsp of salt. Stir once, cover, and cook over very low heat for 18 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining 3 tbsp of olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced onion with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring every 5 minutes, for 25-30 minutes until deeply golden and sweet. Increase the heat to medium-high for the last 3 minutes if you want crisp edges.
Fluff the lentils and rice with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning. Pile onto a platter and top with the caramelised onions and their oil.

items.symptom: Rice not cooked through but lentils are done.
items.cause: Not enough liquid or heat too low.
items.fix: Add 100 ml of boiling water, replace the lid, and cook for a further 5 minutes.

items.symptom: Caramelised onions pale and soft rather than golden.
items.fix: Increase to medium heat and stir less frequently so the onions make contact with the hot pan for longer.
